messages:
maria: Kicking off security acceptance for the new GPU region cluster (eu3-gpu). Focus: IAM roles, secrets, KMS/HSM integration, policy checks. Need a short checklist + quick validation commands.
ryan: +1. Can we make this a lightweight gate we can run during handoff?
nadia: I can draft the checklist. Quick notes: ensure workload identities are used (no static creds), KMS keys are customer-managed, and HSM usage is documented for sensitive keys.
maria: Perfect. Also include cost/ops note about HSM — curious if we can recommend a fallback that doesn't force HSM for dev clusters.
ashley: Dev clusters should use envelope encryption with cloud KMS (non-HSM) and have a clearly labeled key 'redwood/dev/*'. Prod must require HSM-backed keys and rotate annually.
ryan: Here are the acceptance gates I usually run: 1) IAM: no role with iam:PassRole or wide admin attached to node pools. 2) Secrets: all secrets in vault/secret-store; no secrets in plain k8s secrets. 3) KMS: key is CMK and has proper key policy to allow service account. 4) Networking: control plane only accessible from corp VPC + peering checks.
ashley: I'll paste two quick validation commands we use:
```
# verify there are no k8s secrets labeled plaintext
kubectl get secrets --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["redwood.com/plaintext"]) | {ns: .metadata.namespace, name: .metadata.name}'
# ensure no pod uses hostNetwork when not allowed
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.hostNetwork}\\n{end}' | grep true || echo "no hostNetwork pods"
```
ryan: For KMS we run a simple envelope test: encrypt/decrypt a short blob with the cluster service account to ensure permissions are correct. Example (GCP style):
```
# create encrypted blob
echo -n 'sanity-check' | gcloud kms encrypt --key=projects/PROJECT/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ck --keyring=kr --location=LOCATION --ciphertext-file=- | base64
# decrypt with the same service account context
```
nadia: For AWS it's `aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/ck --plaintext ...` and ensure the IAM principal has kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt/grant usage. Also check no key policy allows `Principal: *`.
infra-bot: policy-scan: IAM policies scanned for eu3-gpu - 12 bindings, 2 warnings (iam:PassRole on role/job-runner).
maria: infra-bot flagged a PassRole warning — can someone investigate the job-runner role access?
ryan: Looking. That PassRole binding comes from an old deploy pipeline. We should change pipeline to use a limited role and add a specific `iam:PassRole` constraint to only allow `roles/limited-deployer`.
nadia: Checklist draft (short):
- IAM: list of service accounts + roles (attach least-privilege)
- Secrets: all secrets in Vault/ExternalSecret synced; encrypted at rest by KMS
- KMS/HSM: key ARN present, key policy restricted, HSM usage documented for prod
- Network: private control plane, restricted egress rules, VPC peering audit
- Pod security: PSP/psp replacement enabled, hostNetwork forbidden, privileged false
- Audit & logging: audit logs shipped to immutable storage, alert rule exists for key policy changes
- Cost notes: HSM enabled for prod only — estimate monthly cost and include in handoff
- Signoff: infra, security, and oncall approval

maria: Good. Add a small validation script for KMS key policy check (IAM binding absence and presence).
ashley: Example key policy grep for GCP: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY --location=LOC --keyring=KR | grep "serviceAccount:svc-prod@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"`
ryan: For AWS policies: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id KEYID --policy-name default | jq .` then check for `"Principal": {}` emptiness.
ops-oncall: From oncall perspective: please ensure emergency decryption workflow exists (doc link: https://internal.redwood/ops/kms-emergency). Also add a circuit-breaker: automated fallback to a read-only key if KMS becomes unavailable.
maria: Noted. Nadia, can you add the emergency doc link into the checklist and an ops step?
nadia: Done. Also adding a little test to ensure nodes cannot assume cluster-admin by default: `kubectl auth can-i '*' '*' --as=system:node:node-name` should be false.
infra-bot: ci-security: secrets-scan completed - 0 plaintext secrets found in repo or cluster manifests.
maria: Great. Last thing: cost/project tagging. Make sure KMS keys have labels/tags with project/team and environment. Ops needs tags to show HSM spend.
ryan: I'll remove the PassRole binding and create a scoped role this morning, then run the full checklist.
ops-oncall: Once checks pass, I'll give final signoff and we can hand it to product for enablement.
maria: Thanks everyone — I'll consolidate this thread into the handoff doc and attach the checklist + commands. If anyone wants to add a 2-line snippet for their environment (AWS/GCP), drop it here.
ashley: Dropping AWS snippet for HSM-enabled key creation: `aws kms create-key --origin AWS_CLOUDHSM --description "redwood/prod/eu3"` and then `aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id <id>`
ryan: I'll post the pipeline change PR shortly.
ops-oncall: signing off pending PR and infra-bot clean scan.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: smoke test started for eu3-gpu cluster (smoke-20260318). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/2345
maria: Closing thread for now — will update handoff doc after PR merge. :thumbsup:"
